take: US refinery utilisation averaged above 95% of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998, which underpins a heavy crude run-rate and keeps product supply ample into winter. The Iran war and the loss of Middle East LNG have forced Europe and Asia to lean harder on other gas sources, with Colombia importing more LNG as domestic production falls, tightening the global gas balance and spilling into fuel-switching economics for distillates. The flow angle sits in diesel: a Malta-flagged tanker left Primorsk on 22 October with nearly 40,000 tonnes of ultra-low-sulphur diesel bound for the US, a legal hot potato with a five-year fuse that could distort transatlantic arbitrage and product positioning. The cross-market link is freight and carbon: whatever the IMO decides in December, a broker will reprice a dry bulk trip the next morning, shifting which line of the fixture carries the carbon cost and how much. Watch the FOMC statement fallout and the dollar for its pass-through into bunker and freight economics, alongside any further Gulf supply disruption headlines.
